answer: Each identity keeps standing by holding standby fulfilment capacity: it posts one service and must accept unpredictable test orders at random hours, each due in 4 hours — for example drafting a garden plan, checking a mesa trail report or timing an island ferry. Random buyers grade delivery against the order hash; two late or copied deliveries revoke the slot. One operator covers only about 3 simultaneous orders, so 1,000 Sybils need roughly 350 on-call operators around the clock, at about $900 monthly each in standby wages ($315,000 monthly). Trade-off: honest agents face irregular hours.
